units.title: In-game saves: the 128 KB flash chip, kept in a .sav
units.detail: Emerald and its hacks save to a 128 KB flash chip (Macronix/Sanyo command protocol, two banks), not the plain 64 KB SRAM the bus has now, so an in-game save goes nowhere. Detect the save type, emulate the chip's commands and IDs, and keep it in <rom>.sav beside the ROM, written on change and readable by mGBA (and mGBA's .sav read back: ~/ROMs/gba/Emerald Rogue.sav). Check: save in Emerald, restart, Continue loads it; the same .sav loads in mGBA.

record.evidence: desktop::sav_file keeps ROM.sav (mGBA sizes, RTC trailer kept, written 30 frames after a change and on exit). Emerald Rogue: mGBA's own .sav gives Continue (player meadow) in ours; an in-game Save in ours wrote slot A (counter 4); with slot B wiped, Continue reaches the overworld in mGBA (mgba-dump --save) and ours, same frame-2000 hash fe4a369644557fb2. just check passes after merging main.

notes.text: Checked on Emerald Rogue (same flash library as Emerald); vanilla Emerald has no save to start from and a new game is a long route. Window play writes ~/ROMs/gba/<rom>.sav itself; test on /tmp copies with --save FILE.
The chip itself (ID, commands, banks, in memory) is now {unit:shared/flash-chip}, which this needs; this unit keeps the .sav file, its detection and mGBA interop.

units.title: Controller input, Steam Deck buttons mapped to the GBA's
units.detail: The desktop window (minifb) reads only the keyboard. Read gamepads (gilrs or SDL2's game controller API; research which runs best under Steam Input in Game Mode) and map them to the GBA keys, L/R to the shoulders, with a hotplug-safe default mapping and a config file to change it. Leave the keyboard working. Check: a test feeds gamepad events and sees KEYINPUT change; june's bench check on the Deck goes in the Deck gate.

record.evidence: gilrs pads in crates/desktop/src/gamepad.rs; tests gamepad_events_reach_keyinput (fed pad events change KEYINPUT over machine frames), gamepads_and_hotplug, gamepad_mappings pass; just check green; gilrs sees quack's Xbox 360 pad. Deck bench check is the play gate's.

notes.text: Stretch goals add macOS and Windows and per-ROM remapping later ({unit:stretch/remap}): pick an input library that works on all three and a mapping format that can take per-ROM overrides.

units.title: Fast-forward: a held or toggled speed-up
units.detail: A button (and key) that runs frames unthrottled or at a set multiple, with audio either sped up or muted rather than crackling, and frame pacing back to a steady 59.73 Hz when released. Check: a test runs N frames under fast-forward in under N/60 s of wall-clock and the frames match a normal run's.

record.evidence: just check passes. Test fast_forward_runs_fast_and_frames_match: 60 frames paced at 59.73 Hz take >=0.99 s; under fast-forward (unthrottled and 4x) <1 s with identical per-frame hashes; fast_forward_mutes_and_sound_comes_back: queue empty during FF, refills after. Real window (cu session, agb sound ROM, 600 frames, --mute): 10.15 s normal, 0.59 s FF, 2.60 s at 4x, hash 756cb3912b8a9443 in all and headless.

notes.text: With sound on, fast-forward was tested only through a player no device drains (test), not a real device: just audio-window doesn't take --fast-forward yet. Pad defaults: rthumb held, lthumb toggles.

units.title: Save states of our own: quick save and load slots
units.detail: Write and read our own save states (all of Machine at a frame boundary, versioned), to slots beside the ROM, bound to buttons. Builds on loading mGBA's states. Check: save at frame N, run on, load, and frames N..N+600 match the first run's hashes exactly, in the recompiled build.

record.evidence: runtime::snap saves all of Machine (cart save included) versioned with ROM and payload CRC-32s; desktop --state-out/--state-at/--state, slots ROM.state1-4 (Shift+F1-4 save, F1-4 load, pad west/north). just own-state-check on Emerald: state at 5400 and at 150 (363 distinct frames), 600 frames from it hash as straight through, interpreter and recompiled; just check passes.

notes.text: Window keys and pad buttons for slots are unit-tested (Slots, files round trip) but weren't tried in a real window or on the Deck. Loading a state also puts back its cart save (as mGBA does) and the .sav is rewritten.

units.title: Rewind: step back through recent frames
units.detail: A ring buffer of states (every few frames, delta-compressed if memory needs it) and a held button that plays it backwards. Say the memory per minute of rewind and keep it under a set cap on the Deck's 16 GB. Check: rewind 5 s, then let it run, and the frames match a run that was never rewound from that point.

record.evidence: just rewind-check on Pokemon Emerald, rewinding 300 frames (5 s) at frame 900 then running to 1200: all 1800 shown frames hash as the straight run, interpreter and recompiled, both with no input (180 distinct frames) and with start/a presses. Memory measured per minute of rewind: 2-31 MB over six ROMs, cap 256 MB (--rewind-mb). just check passes after merging main.

notes.text: Rewind (R key, right stick left) was only tested headless (--rewind F+N, unit tests); not yet held in a real window or on the Deck. Rewinding also rolls the cartridge save back and marks the .sav to be rewritten.

units.title: A Steam Deck build that runs in Game Mode
units.detail: A recompiled game as one x86_64 Linux binary that runs on SteamOS with no install step: fullscreen at the Deck's 1280x800 with aspect-correct scaling, added as a non-Steam game, audio through PipeWire. A just recipe builds one for a given hack, and the unit says what june copies to the Deck. Check: the binary runs fullscreen with no missing libraries in a clean SteamOS-like container.

record.evidence: just deck-build on Emerald Rogue made out/deck/emerald-rogue (96 MB stripped binary, ROM, play.sh, README with Game Mode steps; links only libudev/libasound/libgcc_s/libc/libm, glibc 2.34). just deck-check emerald-rogue 20: ran 20 s via play.sh in a clean podman Arch container on 1280x800 Xvfb, exit 0, ldd nothing missing, window 1280x800+0+0, picture at 5x between black bars (rerun on gba-cart1 after merging main). In cu KWin sessions (X11 and Wayland) the window filled 1280x800 and sound reached PipeWire's null sink through the ALSA plugin, 0 underruns. Not yet tried on a real Deck.

notes.text: June copies out/deck/<name>/ (from just deck-build ROM) to the Deck and adds play.sh as a non-Steam game; its README.txt has the steps. Only tested in containers and headless KWin, not on a real Deck or under gamescope.
gilrs (gamepads) links libudev.so.1 at run time: present on SteamOS, but the clean-container check must include it. Building needs libudev's pkg-config file (systemd-devel).

units.title: Back up the cartridge save each time the game closes
units.detail: From june's play test ({unit:deck/play-gate}). Each time a window build closes (Escape, the window's X, Steam's Exit game), copy the cartridge save (ROM.sav, the mGBA .sav) to a timestamped file in a backups folder beside it, e.g. saves/<game>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.sav, so a bad save or a mistaken state load can be undone. Skip it when the game kept no .sav (--no-save, or nothing saved yet) and when the save hasn't changed since the newest backup. Make sure the pending write of the .sav (written a moment after the game saves) is flushed first, so the backup holds the latest save. Say where backups go in the Deck README and --help.

record.evidence: Window exit now flushes the .sav then copies it to saves/NAME-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.sav beside it (local time), skipped with no .sav or when the newest backup is identical. Test sav_backups_on_exit; offscreen window runs on gba-tests sram.gba: first close backed up, unchanged second skipped, SIGTERM exit backed up. --help and Deck README updated; just check passes after merging main.

units.title: Prune the oldest save backups past 1 GB
units.detail: From june's play test ({unit:deck/play-gate}). When the save-backups folder ({unit:deck/save-backup-on-exit}) grows past about 1 GB, delete the oldest backups until it is under, but never a game's newest backup: every game that has backups keeps at least its latest one. Check on exit, after writing the new backup. Saves are 128 KB, so this takes thousands of sessions to matter; keep it simple. A test covers it: several games' backups over the cap, the oldest go, each game's newest stays.

record.evidence: sav_file::prune runs on exit after the backup (lib.rs), deleting the oldest saves/ backups until they total under 1 GiB, keeping each game's newest. Test sav_backups_pruned_past_cap: three games over the cap, oldest four go, each newest stays, non-backups untouched. just check passes.

units.title: Undo loading a save state
units.detail: From june's play test ({unit:deck/play-gate}). Loading a save state throws away the game as it was; let the player undo the load and get back to where they were just before it (as mGBA's 'undo load state'). Rewind's history already holds that moment, so this may be keeping the pre-load snapshot. june has user-interface ideas for how this should look and feel: ask them (just ask) before settling the design, and don't build a UI they haven't seen.

record.evidence: Built june's choice (menu row plus a key): F5 and the menu's 'Undo load state' row (greyed and skipped when nothing to undo) restore the game from before the last load, once; title says 'load undone'. just check passes after merging main; menu/slot tests cover it; live under headless gamescope a pad script saved, loaded, undid via the menu (stderr: load undone). Branch commits 8e888d4, 5a37d4f.

notes.text: Mechanism committed on branch unit/deck/undo-load-state (a0b0a20): slots::act keeps pre-load state, Action::UndoLoad restores once; tested in slot_states. Only the trigger/UI is left, per june's answer to the undo-load question.

The window's close button and Steam's Exit game still quit at once (and still write the .sav).

units.title: Fast-forward draws about 50 frames a second, not 60
units.detail: In the on-Deck play test ({unit:deck/deck-gate}) presents read p50 19.9 ms, p99 20.8, but june was on 2.5x fast-forward most of the session, and that explains it: fast-forward redraws when at least 1/DRAW_HZ (1/60 s) has passed since the last draw (crates/desktop/src/platform.rs, near line 249). At 2.5x a GBA frame finishes every 6.7 ms, so the first frame past 16.7 ms comes at 20.1 ms: about 50 draws a second. Other speeds land at other uneven rates. Not a Deck problem. Fix: put the draws on a fixed 60 Hz schedule (advance the deadline by 1/60 s each draw, catching up if it falls behind) rather than counting from the last draw, so fast-forward shows close to 60 a second at any speed; check with the presents line at 2.5x (p50 near 16.7 ms). The exit report doesn't separate normal-speed presents from fast-forward ones, so the Deck's pacing at 1x wasn't measured on its own; consider reporting fast-forward presents separately, as the menu's are (with the menu:).

record.evidence: Fast-forward redraws on a fixed 60 Hz schedule (fast::DrawPacer). Test fast_forward_draws_sixty_a_second on a made-up clock: 1.5x/2.5x/4x/16x mean gap 16.7 ms. Live under headless gamescope 1280x800, 900 frames: new 'fast-forward:' presents line, mean 16.7 ms at 2.5x (p50 14.8, p99 21.9), 1.5x and 4x also 16.7; was 20.1 at 2.5x. just check passes; main merged (up to date).

notes.text: Retro 2026-10-24: lanes only measured pacing at 1x, so this got to the Deck. Besides the live presents check, add a desktop unit test on the fake clock: at 1.5x, 2.5x and 4x, draws come about every 16.7 ms.

units.title: Resume where you left off, safe across a crash
units.detail: june, 2026-10-29: on by default, with a menu setting to turn it off. Because she'll come to trust it, it must survive a crash or a pulled battery: take an auto state every few seconds of play (1 to 5 s, cheap with rewind's delta states), written to a temp file and renamed so a crash mid-write never leaves a broken one, keeping the one before; take one on quit too. At launch, resume from it straight away. Separate from the four manual slots. Check: play, kill -9 the process, relaunch, and it resumes within a few seconds of where it was; also quit normally and relaunch. See docs/research/emulator-ux.md.

record.evidence: Earlier session's window check stands (Kirby & the Amazing Mirror in a private cu session: kill -9 with ROM.resume 1.1 s old, relaunch resumed in the same spot; Ctrl+Q wrote one at quit and relaunch resumed there; unit tests auto_states_resume_and_keep_the_newer_sav). units.title: Launch cleanly from ES-DE and other frontends
units.detail: june, 2026-10-29: no game library of our own; fit into ES-DE and launchers like it. Command-line flags for where saves, states and settings live, and a fallback so switching launchers never strands a save: one fixed home per game keyed by the ROM's hash (e.g. under the XDG data dir), flags override it, and a save found in an older place (beside the ROM or executable) is picked up, not shadowed. Plus a sample ES-DE system entry. Ask june before settling the location rule. See docs/research/emulator-ux.md.

record.evidence: Added --config-dir (gamepad::set_config_dir, test config_dir_flag) and deploy/es-de/ es_systems.xml + es_find_rules.xml (xmllint ok), documented in docs/tools/commands.md. End-to-end launch as ES-DE runs it: sh -c 'gbaa-desktop --fullscreen --config-dir CFG --frames 120 "ROMs/gba/Save Test (SRAM).gba"' from /, scratch HOME/XDG, SDL offscreen: exit 0, ROM.sav copied in to ~/.local/share/gbaa/saves/save-test-sram/save-test-sram.sav (cmp same) with a backup; 2nd run with a new ROM.sav beside left the folder's save alone; a bad line in CFG/settings.conf was reported by path, so --config-dir is read. just check passes before and after merging origin/main.

notes.text: 2026-10-30 june settled saves: NOT keyed by ROM hash. The flags, folders and move-in are now their own units (needs); this unit is the ES-DE sample entry and an end-to-end launch check using them, plus --config-dir. Follow docs/save-locations-design.md over the What above.

No code yet. Saves/states/resume all use rom.with_extension in sav_file.rs, slots.rs, resume.rs; --save already exists (lib.rs ~687 defaults it via sav_file::beside). Build flags + fallback per june's answer to the save-location question; ES-DE sample independent.

units.title: Frame blending for games that flicker, as a toggle
units.detail: From june's Kirby & the Amazing Mirror playtest (2026-10-29): 'the flashing is awful, I hate GBA flashing'. Some games draw sprites on alternate frames and count on the slow LCD to blend them. Add frame blending (mix each frame with the last), a Display row in the menu and a settings key, off by default so the picture stays as {d:keep-the-picture-as-it-is-no-colour-correction} keeps it; maybe on per game where a game flickers (Kirby). docs/research/emulator-ux.md covers what others do. Check: a test on the blend; screenshots of Kirby's flicker off and on; just check.

units.title: A state from another ROM that crashes undoes its load

Unit tests cover crash and play-on. units.title: Single-player window: hand frames to the display evenly
units.detail: The netplay feel sim (2026-11-08, {unit:multiplayer/rollback-feel-sim}) found a frame handed to the window when done meets the 60 Hz display unevenly: each finish that crosses a refresh makes a doubled and a skipped frame. Netplay now presents 8 ms into the turn (gbaa-desktop --present-ms). The single-player loop still hands frames over when done; its costs vary less, so measure first (the window's present gaps, or a sim like netplay::feel's), then do the same if it shows. docs/research/multiplayer.md, Feel.
